title: Port Security: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Anyone can plug a laptop into a spare wall port. And just like that, they're on your network. Port security is the guard on the door.

lines.t: Any laptop, any spare wall port
Port security is the guard on the door

scenes.heading: The security guard
scenes.narration: Think of an apartment where a guard checks every visitor. The guard knows the allowed devices by their M A C address. By default, only one device per port is allowed. Sticky learning means the guard memorises the first visitor. But the guard's notebook is only kept if you save the config.

scenes.heading: Three responses
scenes.narration: When an unknown device shows up, you choose the response. Protect silently drops the frames. Restrict drops them and logs a warning. Shutdown, the default, locks the door completely.

scenes.heading: The configuration
scenes.narration: Here's the config. Turn it on for the port. Set how many devices are allowed. Choose what happens on a violation. And verify with show port security.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three slip-ups. Protect mode doesn't send any log message. Sticky addresses aren't saved until you save the config. And the default maximum is one address, not zero.

items.wrong: Protect mode sends a syslog message

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva port security lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Port security limits which devices can use a port. The default is one device, and the default response is shutdown. Sticky addresses need saving to survive a reboot. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva port security lab.

points.t: Limits which devices may use a port
